intro: To use the navigation pane in Word on Mac, open the View menu and choose Navigation Pane, then click a heading to jump to that section. The pane only lists headings that use heading styles, so apply Heading 1, 2, or 3 first with ⌘⌥1, ⌘⌥2, or ⌘⌥3.
tldr: Open View > Navigation Pane. Some builds and older guides call it Sidebar or Document Map.
Headings appear only when you use heading styles. Apply them with ⌘⌥1, ⌘⌥2, or ⌘⌥3.
You cannot drag headings to reorder them in the Mac pane. Use Outline view for that.
Search with ⌘F. Microsoft's Mac shortcut list has no key that opens the pane itself.

blocks.text: The navigation pane is the outline that sits on the left side of a Word document. It lists your headings, shows thumbnails of your pages, and lets you search. On a long report, thesis, or policy document, it saves a lot of scrolling. When the list comes up empty, the cause is usually the heading style, and that fix takes a minute. This page covers how to open the pane, what each view does, why headings go missing, and where Microsoft's documentation falls short for Mac.
Open the navigation pane in Word on Mac

Microsoft's main Navigation pane article is written for Windows. It says the Mac and web versions behave differently, but it does not explain how. The article lists Word for Microsoft 365, Word 2024, 2021, 2019, and 2016, and no Mac version. Because of that gap, the menu label changes from one guide to the next. Start with View > Navigation Pane. If that item is not on your menu, look for one of the other names in the list below.

items: View > Navigation Pane: the path in the 2026 iTechGuides guide.
View tab > Show > Navigation Pane: a checkbox, as described in a 2021 SUNY Oswego guide.
View > Sidebar: the label in a 2014 Royal Wise guide. Treat it as an older name.
View > Document Map: named by iTechGuides as an alternative, depending on your build.
View > Outline: opens Outline view, a different tool. You use it to reorder headings.

blocks.text: Some builds put the control on the View tab in the ribbon. The Oswego guide describes a Show group with a Navigation Pane checkbox. Check the box to open the outline on the left. Clear it to close the pane again. Either route gives you the same pane once it is open.
What each view shows in the pane

The pane has tabs across the top. Microsoft's Windows article names three of them: Headings, Pages, and Results. Headings is the outline of your document. Pages shows a small preview of each page, so you can jump by looking. Results lists every match when you type a search term. Mac builds may use different tab names, so compare what you see with the table.

rows: Your document outline, built from heading styles
Click a heading to jump. Click the arrow beside it to show subheadings.
Click a thumbnail to jump to that page.
Every match for the text you typed in search
Click each match to move through the document.

Check which tabs your build shows, because names and order may differ.

blocks.text: A 2014 guide from Royal Wise says the pane can act as a find and replace tool. It also says search matches show highlighted in yellow. That guide was last updated in June 2014, so test those details on your own copy. The basic job of the pane stays the same. It shows structure and lets you move around.
Why your headings do not appear in the pane

The pane builds its list from heading styles. Microsoft says headings appear only when heading styles are applied. Bold text does not count, and neither does a bigger font. A line that looks like a heading to you can be invisible to the pane. Check that first. It is the fastest fix on the list.

items: Bold text or a larger font with no heading style: the pane skips it.
A heading inside a table, text box, header, or footer: Microsoft says these do not appear.
A custom style with no Outline Level: Office Watch's April 2026 article says styles with an Outline Level appear in the pane.
A document with no heading structure at all: Oswego notes the pane is only effective when a heading structure is in place.

blocks.text: To check any line, click into it and look at the Styles gallery on the Home tab. If it reads Normal, the pane will ignore that line. Change it to Heading 1, Heading 2, or Heading 3. Then return to the pane and confirm the line shows up.
Apply heading styles with keyboard shortcuts

Select a heading line and press ⌘⌥1 for Heading 1, ⌘⌥2 for Heading 2, or ⌘⌥3 for Heading 3. Microsoft's Mac shortcut page lists these three combinations. Use Heading 1 for chapter titles, Heading 2 for sections inside a chapter, and Heading 3 for subsections. The pane then nests them the same way, so you can expand and collapse each level.

Work through the document once from top to bottom. Give each section a heading style. Then open the pane and check that every section appears in order. If one is missing, look at its style before you change anything else.
Reorder headings on a Mac

You cannot drag headings to reorder them in the Mac navigation pane, according to the sources checked for this page. A 2021 answer from an MVP and a 2022 Microsoft Q&A thread both say the Mac pane has never moved headings. The 2022 moderator also pointed to Outline view, where drag and drop works. Neither source confirms whether this has changed in 2026, so test it on your build.

To reorder, choose View > Outline. Drag a heading to move that section. Then switch back to Print Layout and check the page breaks and the flow of the text. Outline view is the tool for moving sections. The pane is the tool for finding them.

items: ⌃⇧← or ⌃⇧→: promote or demote the heading you are on.
⌘⇧N: demote a heading to body text.
⌃⇧+ or ⌃⇧-: expand or collapse the outline.
⌃⇧↑ or ⌃⇧↓: move paragraphs up or down. macOS also uses these keys, so they can conflict.

blocks.text: Microsoft lists these shortcuts for Outline view only. Press them in Print Layout and they will not move your headings. Microsoft's page marks the arrow-key conflicts with an asterisk, so check that the macOS shortcut is not capturing the keys first.

blocks.title: Use the pane to find, Outline view to move
blocks.text: The pane is quick for jumping to a section. Outline view is better for rearranging. Switch between the two while you edit.
Search and Go To from the pane

Press ⌘F to move focus to the in-document search box. Microsoft's Mac page says this. It does not say that ⌘F also opens the navigation pane, so test that on your copy. Control+H opens the Find and Replace pane. ⌘⌥G or F5 opens Go To. ⇧F5 returns you to the last change or insertion point. Use these together with the pane when a document is long.
Microsoft notes that some shortcuts need the fn key on some MacBooks. If a shortcut does nothing, try holding fn first. Then check whether macOS already uses that key combination for something else.
Known bug: headings two levels below

In a June 2025 Microsoft Q&A thread, a user on Word for Mac 16.98 reported that selecting a level in the pane highlighted a heading two levels below it. The problem showed up in large documents with custom multilevel lists. A Microsoft staff member called it primarily a Word for Mac defect. The thread does not list a confirmed fix.

If you hit this bug, start by checking the Outline Level for the heading in Format > Paragraph. The thread also suggests ⌘⌥Q to reset the paragraph. Use that with care. In the thread, a staff workaround of redefining the list removed the numbering for the person who posted it. Make changes on a copy first.

blocks.title: Test before you redefine lists
blocks.text: Redefining a multilevel list can remove numbering. Save a copy of the document before you try any list workaround.
Mistakes people make with the Mac pane

The first mistake is assuming the pane reads formatting. It reads styles. The second is using a heading style inside a table or header and expecting it to appear in the pane. The third is pasting text from a web page, which can bring in direct formatting that does not match the heading style. Paste as plain text, then apply the heading style again.

The fourth mistake is trusting an old guide for menu labels. The fifth is ignoring your build number. The latest Office for Mac release is 16.114.4, build 26110224, dated November 4, 2026. Open Word > About Word to see your version before you compare your screen with any guide.
Check your build before you trust a menu label

Microsoft's release notes for Word on Mac from October and November 2026 list quality and performance improvements only. None of those entries mention the pane, headings, outline, or sidebar. The most recent Word feature entry on that page is from July 15, 2025, and it covers the Copilot icon. A missing pane is more likely to come from a view setting or a style problem than from a recent release change.
Why clear headings matter beyond Word

Headings matter for people who use screen readers. In WebAIM's Screen Reader User Survey #10, run from December 2023 to January 2024, 71.6% of respondents said they would first navigate through headings on a lengthy web page. That survey covers web pages, not Word files. It still shows why clear heading structure helps people find their place fast.

WebAIM's Survey #11, run from July to August 2026, asked about Word documents. Of those who answered, 31.1% said Word documents are very or somewhat likely to pose significant accessibility issues for them. For PDFs, the figure was 85.6%. Heading styles are one of the simplest fixes you control inside Word.
Next steps once the pane works

Once the headings show, you can build on them. A table of contents uses the same heading styles, so the work you did here feeds into it. See [how to insert a table of contents in Word on Mac](/how-to/insert-a-table-of-contents-in-word). If others will review your draft, [turn on Track Changes](/how-to/turn-on-track-changes-in-word) before you start editing.

If the pane still misbehaves after these steps, save a copy of the file and test on a short sample. That shows whether the problem is in the document or in the app. Write down your build number when you report it to Microsoft through Word's feedback menu.

faq.question: Is there a keyboard shortcut to open the navigation pane in Word on Mac?
faq.answer: Microsoft's Mac shortcut list does not show one for opening the pane. ⌘F moves focus to the in-document search box, and ⌃H opens Find and Replace. Test whether ⌘F also opens the pane on your build, because Microsoft does not say.

faq.question: Why is my navigation pane empty on a Mac?
faq.answer: The pane builds its list from heading styles. Text that is only bold or large does not count. Select the line and press ⌘⌥1, ⌘⌥2, or ⌘⌥3. Headings inside tables, text boxes, headers, and footers also stay out of the list.

faq.question: Can I drag headings to reorder them in the Mac navigation pane?
faq.answer: Not in the pane, according to a 2021 MVP answer and a 2022 Microsoft Q&A thread. Use View > Outline instead, where drag and drop works. Neither source confirms the 2026 status, so check your build.

faq.question: Does the navigation pane work the same in Word for the web?
faq.answer: Microsoft says the behavior differs on Mac and on the web, but it does not explain how. A third-party guide dated August 10, 2026 says the web app has View > Navigation Pane in Editing view. Verify that in your browser before you rely on it.

faq.question: Why does the pane show a heading two levels below the one I picked?
faq.answer: A June 2025 Microsoft Q&A thread reports this on Word for Mac 16.98 in large documents with custom multilevel lists. Staff called it primarily a Word for Mac defect. Check the Outline Level in Format > Paragraph. That thread lists no confirmed fix.

faq.question: Is the navigation pane on Mac the same as on Windows?
faq.answer: Not quite. Microsoft's article is written for Windows. Office Watch says the Mac version is similar but lacks some options, without naming them. It also says dragging headings to reorder is available in Word for Windows.

faq.question: Which version of Word should I check against this guide?
faq.answer: Microsoft's latest Office for Mac release is 16.114.4, build 26110224, dated November 4, 2026. Open Word > About Word to see your version. If your menu labels differ from this page, trust what your build shows.

steps.name: Open the Word document
steps.text: Open the Word document you want to navigate. The pane only shows the outline of the document in that window, so open the right file first.
steps.tip: If the pane looks wrong, check that you are in the window you think you are in.

steps.name: Open the View menu
steps.text: Click View in the menu bar at the top of the screen. Some builds also show a View tab in the ribbon, and either one leads to the same control.

steps.name: Choose Navigation Pane
steps.text: Click Navigation Pane. The outline opens on the left side of the window. If you see Sidebar or Document Map instead, choose that item.
steps.tip: Mac labels vary by build. iTechGuides says the menu can read Navigation Pane, Document Map, or an equivalent control.

steps.name: Or use the View tab checkbox
steps.text: On the View tab, find the Show group and check Navigation Pane. Clear the box to close the pane. SUNY Oswego's 2021 guide describes this layout.

steps.name: Switch between the pane views
steps.text: Use the tabs at the top of the pane to switch between Headings, Pages, and Results. Headings shows your outline, Pages shows thumbnails, and Results lists search matches.
steps.tip: Older Mac guides show different tab names. Compare what you see with the table in this guide.

steps.name: Jump to a section
steps.text: In Headings view, click any heading. The document scrolls to that spot. Click the small arrow beside a heading to show or hide the subheadings under it.
steps.tip: If a section is missing from the list, check that its heading has a heading style.

steps.name: Search with Command+F
steps.text: Press ⌘F to move focus to the in-document search box. Type a word and check the Results list. Microsoft does not say whether ⌘F also opens the pane, so test it on your copy.
steps.tip: Control+H opens the Find and Replace pane if you need to replace text.

steps.name: Close the pane
steps.text: Choose View > Navigation Pane again to hide the pane. Your headings stay in the document. Only the pane closes.

troubleshooting.problem: The pane is empty even though the document has headings
troubleshooting.fix: Apply a heading style to each heading line. Select the line and press ⌘⌥1, ⌘⌥2, or ⌘⌥3. Then check the Styles gallery on the Home tab to confirm the style name.

troubleshooting.problem: A custom heading style does not appear in the pane
troubleshooting.fix: Open Format > Paragraph and set Outline Level to Level 1, 2, or 3 for that style. Office Watch's April 2026 article says styles with an Outline Level appear in the pane.

troubleshooting.problem: A heading shows two levels below the one I selected
troubleshooting.fix: Check the Outline Level, then try ⌘⌥Q as the Microsoft Q&A thread suggests. Work on a copy. Redefining the list may remove numbering, as it did for the person in that thread.

troubleshooting.problem: Headings will not drag to reorder in the pane
troubleshooting.fix: Switch to Outline view with View > Outline, then drag headings there. The sources checked for this page say the Mac pane does not support dragging.

troubleshooting.problem: The View menu has no Navigation Pane item
troubleshooting.fix: Look for Sidebar or Document Map, which older guides use. Check View > Outline too. Compare your version under Word > About Word with the release history before you assume a fault.
